requirements.summary: useradd created datauser (uid 1000) with home directory; confirmed via `id datauser`.

requirements.requirement: datauser limited to 100MB of storage under /srv/data, enforced by the filesystem itself
requirements.summary: A dedicated XFS filesystem (loop-mounted /srv/data.img) was created and mounted at /srv/data with the prjquota option persisted in /etc/fstab. A correct project-quota mapping was established (/etc/projid: datauser:100, /etc/projects: 100:/srv/data after an initial malformed attempt was immediately corrected) and a 100M hard/soft block limit was applied via xfs_quota, which is a kernel-enforced XFS project quota mechanism rather than an application-level check.

requirements.requirement: Filesystem actually rejects writes by datauser beyond 100MB
requirements.summary: As datauser, a 60MB write succeeded; a second 60MB write failed with ENOSPC exactly at 100MB total usage, and xfs_quota report confirmed used=100M/hard=100M — direct, observed enforcement.

requirements.requirement: Quota configuration survives an unmount/remount cycle
requirements.summary: After removing test files, the filesystem was unmounted and remounted; xfs_quota report still showed the 100M limit for datauser afterward.

requirements.requirement: Filesystem, quota, and enforced limit survive a full node restart (independent restart-evidence protocol)
requirements.summary: Baseline captured pre-reboot (boot_id bfd05127…, healthy quota, successful 10MB write). Reboot was triggered and acknowledged, a connection reset confirmed the node went down, and a subsequent poll showed a new boot_id (594178a7…) with 5s uptime, matching the fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check (before_prepare bfd05127… vs after_executor 594178a7…). Post-reboot, /srv/data auto-remounted via fstab, prior data was intact, the 100M project quota was still active, a 50MB write succeeded, and a 60MB write failed at exactly 100MB with ENOSPC — a full pre/during/post transition was directly observed.

overall_summary: The executor fully satisfied the task: datauser was created and confined to a dedicated XFS filesystem at /srv/data with a kernel-enforced 100MB project quota, with enforcement directly demonstrated both before and after a real node reboot (distinct boot IDs, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots). One minor, self-corrected quota-mapping mistake occurred but left no residue. All temporary test files were cleaned up, and no unnecessary or unexplained mutations remain.
limitations: No independent verification that root or other non-datauser users are unaffected by the quota, though this was not part of the stated requirement.
Reliance on executor-reported command outputs; no independent re-execution of commands was possible from this evaluation.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task or to bounded evidence collection, and all temporary test artifacts were removed. Package installs (xfsprogs, quota) and the loop-mounted XFS filesystem creation were necessary prerequisites. One self-correction occurred: cmd-4b07811acecb4887 wrote /etc/projects and /etc/projid with an incorrect line format (project name where projid was expected), immediately superseded and fixed in cmd-ea4cfcc15e2444c2 with the correct name:projid / projid:path mapping — a low-risk, fully-corrected misstep rather than retained residue. Test files created during quota verification (testfile1/2, healthcheck, post_reboot_ok/fail) were all deleted in cmd-09937335151b46eb and the final cleanup cmd-95fdc02cb7ad4b66, leaving /srv/data empty and quota-configured. No failed services, no unsafe exposure changes (socket diff is only ephemeral ports/PIDs changing across the reboot, not new listeners), and dpkg package health remained clean before and after.
